title: Srimad Bhagavad Gita
author: vyasa
attributionNote: Srimad Bhagavad Gita, attributed to Maharishi Vyaas, as Heritage IITKanpur's Scripture Server catalogues it (SBG), on its own shelf.
description: The Bhagavad Gītā, ascribed to Vyāsa, is a Sanskrit dialogue of some 700 verses in eighteen chapters, set in the Bhīṣma Parva of the Mahābhārata. As the armies stand ready at Kurukṣetra, Arjuna loses heart and asks Kṛṣṇa to teach him. Its subject is right action and knowledge of the Self; its purposes run from steadying a troubled mind to liberation, and it is recited daily as well as studied. It condenses the teaching of the Upaniṣads and stands with them and the Brahma Sūtra as one of the three foundations of Vedānta, read differently by Śaṅkara, Rāmānuja and Madhva. Its reader is anyone who, like Arjuna, stands between duty and doubt and asks to be taught. The summary above is the one Heritage IITKanpur's Scripture Server publishes for the text, and the server's own metadata records it as AI-assisted (claude-opus-5-5); an editor's note for the work itself is still to be written.
historicalContext: Read in the Heritage Scripture Server corpus, which continues the Gita Supersite built at IIT Kanpur: the text, its classical commentaries and the translations the server may serve are held together there.
availabilityNote: The outline is held: 18 chapter(s) and 701 verse address(es), read from the server's own catalogue. The verses are not stored — the licence forbids bulk harvesting and database reconstruction — and are streamed from the API one verse at a time as the work is read, with the attribution HCAL-1.1 requires and the server's own quota and licence notice.

Where the API serves Tier B — the Sanskrit bhāṣya and the AI-generated, community and editorially authored translations — it is displayed non-commercially with attribution and is not relicensed here. Tier C, the authoritative modern-language translations and commentaries, is not served by the API and is not imported.
